=You are an expert recruiter evaluating candidates for TalentRubric Growth Advisors.

--- HIRING CRITERIA ---
Target Role: {{ $('Search Criteria').first().json['Target Role'] }}
Key Skills & Requirements: {{ $('Search Criteria').first().json['Key Skills & Criteria'] }}
Experience Range (Years): {{ $('Search Criteria').first().json['Experience Range (Years)'] }}
Gender Preference: {{ $('Search Criteria').first().json['Gender Preference'] }}

--- FULL JOB DESCRIPTION (may be empty; if present, treat as the authoritative source of requirements) ---
{{ $('Prep JD').first().json.jd_text || 'No job description was provided; use the criteria above only.' }}

--- SCRAPED CANDIDATE CONTENT (each line is one candidate: Title | Snippet | URL) ---
{{ $json.page_text }}

--- INSTRUCTIONS ---
--- SOURCING PLAYBOOK (expert best practices from Glen Cathey / Boolean Black Belt / SocialTalent — apply these) ---
1. PERSON vs JOB POSTING (most important): A real candidate line names an INDIVIDUAL and describes THEIR experience (a personal name, "Senior X at Y", "I built..."). A JOB POSTING describes a role to be filled — signals include "We are looking", "Responsibilities", "Apply", "job description", "N jobs in <city>", salary ranges, and company careers/ATS URLs (careers.*, jobs.*, boards.greenhouse.io, lever.co, workday, indeed, glassdoor, naukri). Any job posting, ATS page, directory or aggregator listing MUST get candidate_name "" and fit_score 0 so it is excluded — never turn a job title into a fake candidate name.
2. SEMANTIC INFERENCE: credit skills and seniority that are implied but not stated verbatim (e.g. "led/mentored a team" implies seniority; "GAAP" implies accounting; "Kubernetes + Terraform" implies DevOps/SRE; "published research" implies depth). Do not require exact keyword matches.
3. TITLE VARIETY: the same role carries many titles across companies — judge on substance, not exact title match (SDE ≈ Software Engineer; SRE ≈ Platform/Infrastructure Engineer; Applied Scientist ≈ ML Engineer). Reward adjacent/synonymous titles that demonstrate the required capability.
4. SIGNAL QUALITY: prefer candidates with concrete, verifiable evidence (specific technologies, measurable impact, named employers) over vague self-description.

Evaluate EVERY candidate line in the scraped content against the HIRING CRITERIA above.
If a FULL JOB DESCRIPTION is provided above, weigh it heavily: match each candidate against the specific responsibilities, must-have skills and seniority described in it, and reference JD-specific requirements in the match_summary. If no job description was provided, rely on the hiring criteria fields only.
If a line is NOT an individual person (e.g. a job posting, a company page, or a hiring announcement), give it fit_score 0 so it can be filtered out.
CRITICAL EXPERIENCE MINIMUM (hard filter): The requested Experience Range defines a MINIMUM number of years of professional experience. Map the lower bound as: '0-2 years' => 0, '3-5 years' => 3, '5-8 years' => 5, '8+ years' => 8. Estimate each candidate's total years of professional experience from their title, snippet and seniority. ANY candidate whose estimated experience is clearly BELOW this minimum MUST be given fit_score 0 (so they are excluded), no matter how well their skills match. Interns, students, fresh graduates and recent grads must get fit_score 0 unless the minimum is 0. Only assign a fit_score of 1 or higher to candidates who meet or exceed the minimum years.
Also factor in the Gender Preference: if a specific gender is requested (Female or Male), prioritize candidates matching it; if 'Any' is selected, ignore gender entirely and rank purely on merit.
Return a JSON ARRAY where each element is one candidate object with exactly these fields:
1. candidate_name (string) - the person's ACTUAL full name exactly as it appears in the source line. If the line does NOT contain an identifiable personal name (e.g. a Hacker News monthly hiring thread, a job posting, a directory or company page), set candidate_name to an empty string "" and give it fit_score 0 so it is excluded. NEVER invent a name such as 'Candidate from July 2019'.
2. current_role (string)
3. fit_score (number 1-10 based on match with target role, skills, experience range & gender preference; use 0 for non-candidates)
4. match_summary (string, 2 sentences explaining fit)
5. key_skills (array of strings)
6. profile_url (string, the LinkedIn/GitHub/source URL for that candidate taken from the URL at the end of their scraped line)
Sort the array by fit_score descending.
You are a JSON generator. Return ONLY a valid, raw JSON array of candidate objects without any markdown code blocks, conversational text, or formatting.

values.html:
💭 Natural Language Search — example prompts (copy & edit)
  • Find a senior backend engineer in Bangalore who knows Java, Spring Boot and Kafka.
  • Senior data engineer in Pune, 5+ years, Spark + Airflow + AWS. Exclude interns and consultants. Search LinkedIn and GitHub.
  • Product designer in Bengaluru with Figma and design-systems experience, 3–5 years. Search Dribbble, Behance and LinkedIn.
  • Lead DevOps / SRE, 8+ years, strong Kubernetes, Terraform and AWS, currently at a product company, in Hyderabad. Prefer GitHub and LinkedIn.
  • Machine learning engineer at a fintech in Mumbai, Master's or PhD, 5+ years with PyTorch and LLMs. Exclude recruiters.
Tips: mention role, skills, location, experience/seniority, exclusions and platforms. Naming LinkedIn / GitHub finds real people; “Google / open web” tends to return job posts. Anything you set in the fields below overrides the AI.
How to fill this form — examples

Natural Language Search (easiest): just describe the role in plain English — e.g. "Senior data engineer in Pune, 5+ yrs, Spark + Airflow + AWS, exclude consultants, search LinkedIn + GitHub". The AI fills the fields below for you. Anything you set explicitly below overrides the AI.

  • Target Role: the job title you are hiring for — Backend Engineer, Data Scientist, Product Manager
  • Key Skills & Criteria: comma-separated must-have skills — Java, Spring Boot, Kafka
  • Job Description (optional, recommended): paste the full JD text or upload the JD as a PDF, Word (.doc/.docx), TXT, RTF, HTML or Markdown file below — the AI scores each candidate against it and pulls extra keywords from it
  • Location: city or region — Bangalore (use the city before any dash)
  • Current Employer (optional): only people at this company — Flipkart
  • Keywords to Exclude (optional): comma-separated terms to filter out — intern, recruiter, freelance
  • Education (optional): minimum qualification — Bachelors / Degree, Masters
  • Expand Job Title Synonyms: choose Yes to also match similar titles (e.g. SDE, Software Developer) — recommended for a wider search
  • Experience Range: the MINIMUM experience required — picking 8+ years excludes anyone below 8 years
  • Target Platforms: where to search — tick LinkedIn + GitHub for best results, or Google / Open Web for a broad search
Example search: Target Role = Backend Engineer, Skills = Java, Spring, Kafka, Location = Bangalore, Exclude = intern, Experience = 3-5 years, Platforms = LinkedIn, GitHub

parameters.jsCode:
const cand = $json || {};
const url = cand.profile_url || '';
const isGH = /github\.com\/[A-Za-z0-9-]+/i.test(url) && !/github\.com\/orgs\//i.test(url);
const isLI = /linkedin\.com/i.test(url);
return { json: {
  rank: cand.rank || '',
  candidate_name: cand.candidate_name || '',
  current_role: cand.current_role || '',
  fit_score: cand.fit_score,
  match_summary: cand.match_summary || '',
  key_skills: Array.isArray(cand.key_skills) ? cand.key_skills.join(', ') : (cand.key_skills || ''),
  profile_url: url,
  verified_gender: '',
  current_company: '',
  verified_title: '',
  location: '',
  pdl_skills: '',
  github_url: isGH ? url : '',
  email: '',
  email_status: '',
  phone: '',
  work_history: '',
  education: '',
  // LinkedIn column: only a real LinkedIn URL, or a non-GitHub fallback (e.g. Stack Overflow) so the URL is not lost
  verified_linkedin: isLI ? url : (isGH ? '' : url),
  enrichment_status: 'skipped - no linkedin (apollo not used)'
} };
